subject: Upscale pipeline + exec readout: capacity, term amendment, and QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veritext.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-09-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Upscale pipeline + exec readout: capacity, term amendment, and QBR scheduling

Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Per our discussion, Veritext is seeing a sustained uptick in transcription/ingestion volume tied to the October product launch and you asked for an initial plan we can pull together to cover the next 6–9 months. High level I propose:

- Short term (30–60 days): temporary burst lanes to cover peak ingest while we lock a committed uplift.
- Mid term (next term): a modest capacity increase (20–30% tokens/day) and a 12-month amendment to preserve preferential pricing.
- Operational: add SRE-led on-call handoff, and a joint QBR within the month to align execs and finalize amendment.

I attached a first-pass mutual action plan and the usage snapshot from August so we have a data baseline. Next steps I suggest this week:

1) Confirm procurement contact who will run the amendment.
2) Lock one of two QBR windows (see proposed slots below).
3) Ben to provide a preliminary uplift estimate (not a formal quote).

Proposed QBR windows (all PT):
- Tue, Sep 21 — 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu, Sep 23 — 14:00–15:00 PT

Let me know which slot works and I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and pre-read. If procurement prefers, we can issue a redline-ready amendment and a DocuSign route for faster execution.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

--
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0198
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veritext.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@veritext.com
Date: 2027-09-13T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upscale pipeline + exec readout: capacity, term amendment, and QBR scheduling

Diego —

Appreciate the quick recap and the MAP/usage files. Procurement (procurement@veritext.com) is the right contact for contracting. A couple notes from our side:

- We have a hard cutover for the new product on Oct 10; between Oct 10–24 we expect ~3x baseline token volume on peak days.
- From an exec perspective, leadership is comfortable with a temporary committed uplift and a 12-month amendment if pricing stays within ~15% of current unit costs.

Procurement asked for a ballpark uplift cost and whether Redwood can do a 60-day effective amendment (start date 2027-09-20) to cover Oct launch while final terms are negotiated. We also have two stakeholders who must attend the QBR: Alicia (VP Product) and Marco (Head of Ops).

I can do Tue Sep 21 at 10:00 PT. Please include a short agenda and a one-page summary for my execs. Also send the DocuSign route for the temporary amendment if you prepare it.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, Platform Partnerships
Veritext Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veritext.com>, procurement@veritext.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Upscale pipeline + exec readout: capacity, term amendment, and QBR scheduling

Looping in pricing and SRE now. Ben — can you run a quick uplift model off the attached usage_snapshot_aug2027.pdf and give Diego a 48-hour ballpark for a 20% and 30% committed uplift (monthly token delta + delta unit cost %)? Keep this as a ballpark for procurement; we can firm it up after SRE confirms runbook impacts.

Laura — can your team confirm whether we can stand up temporary burst lanes for the Oct 10–24 window without an extended lead time, and what the expected latency/SLO impact will be if we route higher concurrency for two weeks? If there are any gating requirements (network, peering, customer-side prep), flag them now so Samantha's ops team can prep.

Diego — I’ll draft the one-page exec summary and a two-slide QBR agenda. I suggest we also put a short pre-call with Laura + Veritext Ops one day before the QBR to validate runbook readiness (suggest Mon Sep 20, 09:00 PT).

Action items and owners (short):
- Ben: uplift cost ballpark (20% & 30%) — owner: Ben, due: 2027-09-16 EOD PT
- Laura: burst feasibility + SLO notes — owner: Laura, due: 2027-09-16 EOD PT
- Diego: calendar invite + draft amendment path (DocuSign) — owner: Diego, due: 2027-09-15
- Marissa: exec one-pager + QBR slides — owner: Marissa, due: 2027-09-18

I’ll cc product/Sales Engineering if we need deeper technical context after Laura’s notes.

--
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Success (Renewals)
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@veritext.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, procurement@veritext.com
Date: 2027-09-16T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Upscale pipeline + exec readout: capacity, term amendment, and QBR scheduling

Thanks team — confirm we’re booked for Tue Sep 21, 10:00–11:00 PT for the QBR. Calendar invite sent with agenda and pre-read (MAP + usage snapshot). Marissa’s one-pager is attached to the invite.

Ben and Laura — appreciate the fast turnaround on the two asks. Per Marissa's plan, procurement and Veritext execs will get a redline-ready temporary amendment for a 60-day effective window starting 2027-09-20 and a concurrent commit uplift proposal (20% and 30%). I’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope for the temporary amendment so procurement can sign ahead of the Oct launch if the numbers are acceptable.

Next internal milestone: exec readout prep (internal only) — Mon Sep 20, 09:00 PT with Laura and Veritext Ops to validate runbook. Diego to own meeting logistics.

Attachments: amendment_summary_draft.docx (outline for temporary amendment).

Looking forward — let’s keep this tight.

--
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
